pr.title: GVN: also turn moves into copies with projections
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: No source-grounded pair with differing defined values can be validated for this PR. The historical change only broadens GVN's StorageRemover from rewriting `Move(local)` to also rewriting `Move(projected_place)` into `Operand::Copy` when the base local is in `reused_locals`. Miri evaluates `Copy` and `Move` operands identically (`eval_operand` treats `Copy(place) | Move(place)` the same and does not invalidate moved-from locations), so a direct literal model always produces the same value. I tested the exact historical `fn1(move (_3.0), _3)` vs corrected `fn1((_3.0), _3)` shape with custom MIR: the corrected version returned 142, while the historical form hit Miri Stacked Borrows UB from the projected-move argument aliasing the same base-local argument. That is not a valid counterexample because both versions must pass Miri. Attempts to make the aliasing observable without UB using an inline interior-mutability cell also remained UB under argument protection (Miri removes a protected argument tag), and a Copy inline `UnsafeCell` type is not expressible in Rust. Using pointer identity would be an address observation, which is explicitly disallowed. So the only differences available are UB or invalid/non-Copy misuse, not defined original/transformed values.

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's StorageRemover rewrote an operand only when it was `Operand::Move(place)` and `place.as_local()` succeeded, i.e. only for a projection-free local: `if let Operand::Move(place) = *operand && let Some(local) = place.as_local() && self.reused_locals.contains(local) { *operand = Operand::Copy(place); }`. Projected moves such as `_3.0` or `(_5 as Err).0` therefore remained `move` operands even when their base local was in `reused_locals`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical pass performed the Move-to-Copy rewrite only for bare locals and did not rewrite projected moves. In `gvn_copy_moves`, after GVN had replaced the copied local `_4` with `_3`, the output was `_5 = fn1(move (_3.0: [u128; 6]), _3)`: one operand still moved out of `_3.0` while the same base local `_3` was passed again. Similarly, the SeparateConstSwitch dump retained `_12 = move ((_5 as Err).0: i32)`, `_10 = move ((_1 as Err).0: i32)`, and `_9 = move ((_1 as Ok).0: i32)`. The corrected behavior rewrites these to copies, e.g. `_5 = fn1((_3.0: [u128; 6]), _3)` and `_12 = ((_5 as Err).0: i32)`, while retaining the guard `!place.is_indirect_first_projection()`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions where GVN has identified a local as reused (`reused_locals`) and an operand moves a place based on that local, including places with field or enum-downcast projections. The regression example uses a tuple `([u128; 6],)`, an array write through a constant index, a tuple copy `d = c`, and `Call(x = fn1(Move(c.0), d), ReturnTo(bb1), UnwindUnreachable())`. The cross-pass example uses enum downcasts such as `((_5 as Err).0: i32)`. Places whose first projection is indirect are outside the copy-rewrite domain.
analysis.summary: Historical GVN bug-fix (body: `Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/120613`) extending StorageRemover's Move-to-Copy rewrite from bare locals to projected places. The old condition `place.as_local()` silently skipped projections, leaving `move (_3.0)` and `move ((_5 as Err).0)` in GVN output even though the base local was reusable. The fix tests `!place.is_indirect_first_projection() && self.reused_locals.contains(place.local)`, so field/downcast projections become copies while indirect first projections remain moves. The updated SeparateConstSwitch dump is a downstream expectation change caused by GVN already removing moves through enum downcasts; it is not a SeparateConstSwitch algorithm change.
analysis.trigger: A `Move` operand names a projected place such as a tuple field `_3.0` or an enum downcast field `(_5 as Err).0`, and the place's base local is a GVN-reused local. The old `place.as_local()` check returns `None`, so the move is not converted to a copy. This becomes observable when GVN also replaces another local with that same base local, yielding simultaneous movement out of a projection and use of the base local.
preconditions: The base `place.local` is present in GVN's `reused_locals`.
The place's first projection is not indirect; field and downcast projections are eligible, while indirect first projections are not.
GVN copy propagation can make another use refer to the same base local, exposing the remaining projected move.
pitfalls: `Place::as_local()` succeeds only for a place with no projections; using it as the reuse test silently excludes `_3.0` and `(_5 as Err).0`.
Do not simply remove the `as_local()` check and convert every move: the accepted condition explicitly excludes places with an indirect first projection via `!place.is_indirect_first_projection()`.
The rewrite must be tied to `reused_locals`; converting arbitrary moves to copies is not justified by this change.
Do not conflate this storage-reuse/copy rewrite with general borrow restrictions or post-copy overwrites; the evidence only supports rewriting moves of reused locals under the projection guard.
A GVN output change can make another pass's MIR-dump expectation stale; the SeparateConstSwitch diff updates are cross-pass test maintenance, not evidence that SeparateConstSwitch itself changed.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `#[custom_mir]` unit test annotated `// unit-test: GVN` and `// EMIT_MIR gvn_copy_moves.fn0.GVN.diff`. Build a local tuple/array, write through a constant index, copy the tuple to another local, then call a function with `Move(c.0)` and the copied local. The GVN dump should show the index folded (`_2[1 of 2] = const 1_u128;`) and the projected operand rendered without `move` (`fn1((_3.0: [u128; 6]), _3)`). Also cover enum downcast projections and preserve moves through indirect first projections. Update cross-pass MIR dumps, such as SeparateConstSwitch, when GVN legitimately removes those projected moves. No compiler execution is claimed here.
